title: Reconcile attribution for embeddings / rerank and non-chat function-invocations to prevent duplicate or missing billing
creator: Priya Patel
description: Summary: We are seeing inconsistent usage accounting for non-chat endpoints that perform embeddings, rerank, or function-invocations (structured outputs). Some requests are under-counted (leading to charge discrepancies and quota gaps) while others are double-counted when the same logical operation traverses the batching layer and then the function-invocation router. Root cause hypothesis: two different metering paths exist — the legacy per-request token counter used by text-generation and the newer event-driven aggregator used by embeddings/rerank. Non-chat structured responses and function-invocations sometimes bypass the canonical tokenization step, and batched operations get assigned attribution keys that disagree with rate-limiter keys. This causes (a) missing increment to customer quota when the event is consumed downstream, and (b) duplicated increments when retries and batched splits both emit usage events. Impact: customer-facing billing mismatches, quota enforcement holes allowing burst overages, and inaccurate per-route latency/cost dashboards. This ticket scopes a reconciliation plan: unify metering contract for non-chat endpoints, add idempotency and canonical attribution keys for batched function-invocations, implement a backfill job to correct historical usage in the billing warehouse for the last 30 days, add tests and observability, and roll out via a canary with automatic fallback to legacy accounting on anomaly detection.
acceptance_criteria:
- All non-chat endpoints (embeddings, rerank, structured function-invocations) emit usage events through the canonical metering gateway with a consistent attribution key (customer_id + request_wave_id + canonical_operation_id).
- Metering pipeline deduplicates by idempotency key so retries and batch splits do not cause duplicate billing.
- Rate-limiter lookup uses the canonical attribution key and denies requests that exceed quota within configured windows.
- Backfill job populates missing/incorrect usage for the selected 30-day window; results verified against sample customer invoices and internal finance reconciliation views.
- Unit/integration tests cover batched embeddings + function-invocation flows.
- Dashboards show drop in discrepancy rate to <0.1% of total usage for reconciled endpoints during a 48hr canary.
- Feature flag exists to toggle the new metering path per-region for rollback if anomalies appear.
implementation_steps: Add canonical metering contract and schema change to include canonical_operation_id and request_wave_id in metering events
Update embedding and rerank service codepaths to call the canonical tokenization function before emitting usage events
Implement idempotency dedupe in the metering aggregator keyed by canonical idempotency key
Modify rate-limiter service to use the canonical attribution key for quota checks and counters
Create a simulation harness that replays 7 days of production traces through the new metering logic to measure delta
Author backfill job to compute delta between legacy accounting and canonical accounting and write corrections to billing warehouse (BigQuery) with audit log
Add unit and integration tests covering: batching split/merge, retry semantics, structured output with function-invocation, and negative cases
Deploy behind feature flag in us-west-2 to a 5% traffic canary; monitor discrepancies and error rates for 48 hours
If canary meets SLOs, increase to 25% then full roll; otherwise rollback using feature flag
Run finance verification and mark ticket DONE once accounting reconciliation is validated and backfill completes
progress_updates: 2025-02-14: Ticket created after incident flag from finance (see attachments). Initial triage concluded duplicate/missing increments as likely root cause.
2025-02-18: Completed audit of metering event schemas across services. Found two different event shapes and two different attribution fields (legacy_request_id vs op_signature).
2025-02-20: Prototype canonical tokenization util implemented and bench-tested locally; preliminary CPU overhead <2% on sample workloads.
2025-02-24: Simulation harness run on a 7-day trace showed a 4.7% discrepancy rate in legacy accounting; canonical path reduces duplicates by ~92% in simulation.
2025-02-26: PRs opened for embedding service and metering aggregator. Backfill design doc drafted (attachments).
2025-02-28: Canaries scheduled for 2025-03-02 in us-west-2 at 5% traffic; migration playbook and rollback steps reviewed with SRE and Finance.
